# Handover — daviesportfolios

> **ARCHIVE, since 2026-09-05.** The live record is now `docs/LEDGER.md`,
> under the ledger protocol in `.agents/skills/ledger/SKILL.md`. Read
> that first on any resume; a pre-commit hook keeps it moving with the
> work. This file keeps the deep history — the decision log below and
> the raw session transcripts — and closed operations move into it from
> the ledger, so the live file stays cheap to read on every wake. It is
> 41k lines: open it when a closed item is reopened or audited, not on
> every start. Everything below describes how it was maintained while it
> WAS the live record, and is kept for that context.

**This file was the running record of work on this repo, and it was
maintained in real time.** Every session updates it as it goes: the plan
before the work, the state as it changes, the reviews as they come back.
The point is that a session can die mid-task — context exhaustion, a
crashed container, a closed tab — and whoever picks it up next, human or
model, can read this file and know exactly where things stand without
reconstructing it from commit messages.

The rule is in `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `working-with-davies`
skill. Update **as you go**, not at the end: an update written after the
session ends is one that never got written.

- **Part 1 — Current state** is the live section. Rewrite it.
- **Part 2 — Decision log** is append-only. Never rewrite a past entry;
  add a new one that supersedes it, and say which.
- **Part 3 — Session transcripts** is the archive. Append, never edit.

Never copy live balances out of this file into new files, issues, or
anything public. The repo is private; this file quotes real positions.

## Repairs that went straight to `main` (2026-08-18)

Four changes bypassed PR #209 because each was actively losing data.

1. **`migrate()`'s sold-out heal was zeroing a live position** (`123985f`).
   It fires on any holding with sells whose lot ledger nets to ≤0, then
   overwrites `shares` with 0, zeroes the cost and strips the ticker out
   of every position. PLTR's ledger is a complete 2024 round trip (6.5
   bought, 6.5 sold) while 55 shares sat in the account — so it deleted
   it, silently, on every reload. Now gated on the BOARD already reading
   ~0 shares, the only case the float-dust bug it was written for ever
   produced.
2. **PLTR put back on the board** (`214626e`, migration `0028`): 55
   shares at 123.29, `closed` removed, ledger intact, restored to the
   `CM` slot the owner named.
3. **The broker may never shrink a position held at two platforms**
   (`517a7d0`, migration `0030`). See the decision log — this reverts
   item 6 of the same day.
4. **The order backfill stops parking, and its fills reach the editor**
   (this session). See "The transaction-history fix" below.
5. **The remove-lot ✕ was outside the modal on every desktop width.**
   Grid children default to `min-width: auto`, so the two `1fr` columns
   refused to shrink below a bare input's ~177px intrinsic width and
   pushed the button 80px past the body. Only the ≤760px stacked layout
   escaped it. Found by measuring the modal in a browser while checking
   the new panel, not by looking at the CSS.

## The share-count overwrite (2026-08-18) — what happened

`123985f` widened the T212 sync from a two-ETF allow-list to every
position the broker reports, which is right: it is what brought PLTR's
55 shares back. Shipped alongside it was a rule that on a ticker's FIRST
sync the broker's share count REPLACES the board's, on the reasoning
that a board excess was stale data.

For this book that reasoning is false. Three holdings sit at Trading 212
*and* elsewhere, and the rule deleted the elsewhere half:

| | board | broker | deleted |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPCX | 130 | 59 | 71 |
| RKLB | 160 | 148.5 | 11.5 |
| HOOD | 50 | 20 | 30 |

The owner's own records for the other platform match the deleted
amounts exactly — SPCX 50 @ 105.40 (2026-04-19) + 21 @ 135 (2026-06-12),
RKLB 11.5 @ 48.18 (2025-11-07), HOOD 30 @ 81.09 (2026-02-02) — and the
board's blended average cost reconciles against broker slice + other
platform to within a few cents on all three. The board was right the
whole time.

The change was also unnecessary. PLTR would have come back in full under
the old rule anyway: `max(0, 0 − 55)` is 0, so the broker's slice is the
whole position when the board reads sold-out.

Reverted in `517a7d0`, pinned by `NEVER shrinks a position held at more
than one platform` in `src/trading212.test.js` with these exact numbers.
Migration `0030` restored the three totals, leaving `t212Shares` at the
broker's true slice so the delta path resumes correctly. Verified in the
database: 130 / 160 / 50 with t212 slices 59 / 148.5 / 20.

## The transaction-history fix (2026-08-18)

The owner: "我点开每个股票的交易记录为什么都只有很久以前的". Three
separate reasons, all now addressed.

1. **Nothing has ever written to the ledger except the owner.**
   `applyTrading212` deliberately `void`s its `orders` argument and
   preserves `lots` / `sells` untouched — the guard put in after the
   original sync destroyed them. So a holding not hand-edited since
   April shows nothing since April.
2. **The order backfill was parked, in both accounts.** `t212_orders`
   held 70 rows, all `buy`, all `invest`, all between 2026-07-20 and
   2026-08-17; ISA had stored nothing at all, ever. Cause:
   `ordersPageShapeMismatch` treated ONE fill it couldn't shape as an
   unreadable page and froze the cursor, discarding the other 49 rows
   with it. The rows it couldn't shape were `negative-quantity` — real
   fills whose quantity arrives signed — and a frozen walk never
   latches `complete`, so the top-up pass that re-reads page one for
   today's fills never runs either. Both fixed: the sign is read as a
   sale with `order.side` overriding it, and a page only freezes when
   NOTHING on it parsed.
3. **Nothing in the app read `t212_orders`.** Even the 70 stored fills
   were invisible. `EditTickerModal` now shows the broker's fills for
   that ticker under the lot grid, ticks the ones the ledger already
   carries, and offers the rest as one click. Read-only until pressed —
   folding them in is the owner's call, not a sync's.

The editor also warns now when the rows account for fewer shares than
the board holds, because **Save recomputes `shares` from the ledger**
(`updateHolding` → `netPosition`). On this book that is a loaded gun: 16
of 26 holdings carry lots short of their board count, so a single Save
on RKLB would have dropped it from 160 to 30.

## The ledger is the broker's history now (2026-08-19)

The owner opened the lot editor and couldn't read it: "两个t212账户的
记录不是已经全都有了吗，为什么会有missing". He was right, and the panel
that asked him to fold fills in one by one was wrong twice over.

**The two records don't correspond row for row.** SPCX carried ONE lot of
`59 @ 144.31` — T212's reported average price, not a trade that ever
happened — while the twelve real fills ran 165.58 down to 115.48 over a
month. A 1:1 matcher makes all twelve look new, so "+ Add 12 missing"
would have booked 118 shares where 59 were held. No tolerance fixes that.

So the refresh tick REBUILDS instead (`applyFillLedgers` in
`src/t212_fills.js`). A synced holding's ledger becomes the broker's own
fills, in date order, at the real prices. Two rules:

1. Only a ticker with a `t212Shares` tag AND fills to its name. A CN fund
   and a cold wallet are untouchable by construction.
2. The result must net to the board's own share count, or nothing is
   written. A half-walked backfill leaves the ledger exactly as it was
   and the editor says the history is still downloading.

`src: 'other'` marks what the broker has no claim over — another
platform's shares, and anything typed into the editor from now on.
Migration `0033` marks the four that predate it (SPCX 50 + 21, RKLB 11.5,
HOOD 30), which are exactly each holding's excess over its broker slice,
so all three still net to 130 / 160 / 50.

**Verified once both walks finished (2026-08-19 00:29).** `invest`
latched at 919 fills, `isa` at 1,054. All **24** Trading 212 holdings
now rebuild — every one of them nets to the board's own share count
exactly, from 2DG.SG's 580 down to VUAA.L's 2.2468. The two that don't
rebuild are the two that shouldn't: `017731` (a CN fund) and `BTC-USD`,
neither of which the broker has ever seen.

**`cost` follows the ledger; `shares` never moves.** The board's figure
was T212's `averagePricePaid` — the average of what was BOUGHT — while
this app's basis is the net-cash model the owner specified. Seventeen of the
twenty-four covered holdings agree to within $20 of total cost. The
whole shift is +$1,831, and ORCL is +$2,007 of it: sold down from 123
fills to 70 shares, $28.68/share apart. He was shown the numbers and
chose to follow the trades.

## The extended-hours board read 0.00 %, and why (2026-08-19)

Every US holding showed exactly 0.00 % under the toggle, and it survived
a hard refresh. Not a missing figure — a real, computed zero, which is
why the em-dash fix (below) didn't touch it.

`applyTrading212` replaces Yahoo's `lastPrice` with the broker's live
quote. That exists for `VUAA.L` / `SAEM.L`, whose free Yahoo feed runs
15-20 minutes behind, and it ran on exactly those two while the sync
covered only them. `123985f` widened the sync to every reported position
and widened this with it. One layer down,
`applyTrading212NightPrice` measures the overnight move against
`lastPrice` as today's regular close — so once the broker's quote WAS
the lastPrice, it compared that quote against itself.

Found by comparing what the browser had SAVED (`lastPrice` and
`extPrice` identical) against what the prices Edge Function returns
directly (different). Scoped back to `T212_LIVE_PRICE_TICKERS`.

Two lessons for the next session:

- A probe that mocks the thing you're debugging proves nothing. The
  first one returned `{holdings: {}, prices: …}`, so `applyTrading212`
  had nothing to overlay and the bug couldn't reproduce.
- `board_data`'s saved prices are real evidence — the fingerprint only
  covers user data, so they're whatever was last written for another
  reason, but when they contradict a live fetch that contradiction is
  the bug.

Alongside it: the heatmap now shows an em dash rather than `+0.00%` when
a row has no extended figure at all, because painting "nobody knows" as
"unchanged" states a fact that isn't one.

## Settled design decisions (do not re-open without asking)

- **The value line is `computeAt(...).value`.** Not a reconstruction,
  not a recorded figure — the identical call the vs-S&P view makes on
  the identical grid. The single most important structural rule here.
- **The recorder records inputs, never answers.** `price_snapshots`
  holds `{ticker → native price}` per 5-minute bucket. The server must
  never learn what the portfolio is worth.
- **Deposits are steps, on frozen FX, over the value line's board
  scope.** An exact FX rate of `1` for a non-USD currency is refused —
  that is the missing-pair fallback that once valued a CNY position at
  seven times its size.
- **`portfolio_snapshots` is retired, not dropped.** Its rows stay for
  reference; nothing reads or writes them.
- **The ledger supplies DATES, the board supplies QUANTITY.**
- **A board position larger than the broker's is another platform's.**

The owner said the scoreboard's $167,003 looked low. It is not a

Other findings that still stand:

- **16 of 26 holdings have lot ledgers short of their board share

  holding has none. Bounded (~$673, lot dates only).

# Part 2 — Decision log

Append-only. Newest last.

### 2026-08-18 — roll `main` back to `8d869fe` rather than patch forward

Thirty commits of chart and T212 work had accumulated without
closed-form fixtures or browser verification, each one patching the
previous. Patching forward from a base that could not be trusted would
have kept compounding it. Cost: the features come back on a PR instead
of being live. Rejected alternative: a force-push, which `CLAUDE.md`
forbids without explicit confirmation and which would have lost the
history the audit needed.

### 2026-08-18 — keep `supabase/migrations/**` out of the rollback

A database cannot be reverted by reverting a file. Deleting a migration
whose version is recorded in the remote history breaks `supabase db
push` permanently. Stated explicitly to the owner rather than done
silently.

### 2026-08-18 — record prices, not portfolio values

Recording the ANSWER forces a second implementation of the ledger maths
onto the server, and the two implementations demonstrably diverged in
production. Recording the INPUTS makes the divergence unreachable, and
is strictly more useful: Yahoo has no 5-minute bars a month back and
none at all for a CN fund or a `.PVT` holding. Cost: past values move if
the ledger is edited retroactively — which matches how the owner
described the feature ("历史数据请根据所有股票的买入时间算出").

### 2026-08-18 — the board's share count outranks the lot ledger

Two independent bugs came from trusting the ledger over the board: the
heal zeroing PLTR, and the deposit line under-reporting by the whole
un-lotted slice. On this book the ledger is routinely incomplete (16 of
26 holdings) while the board's share count is what the broker and the
scoreboard agree on. So: the ledger supplies DATES, the board supplies
QUANTITY, and anything reading lots reconciles the residue rather than
believing the shortfall. Rejected alternative: back-filling the missing
lots, which would invent purchase dates that never happened.

### 2026-08-18 — the panel anchors at its window, the modal at the previous close

`buildTickerSeries`'s 1D branch anchors on the previous close, which is
right for a day chart with a previous-close marker (the ticker modal)
and wrong for a panel whose shortest window is a trailing 24 h measured
from its own first point. Keeping one function and adding an explicit
`anchorAtWindowStart` flag beat forking it: the flag is named after what
it does and both behaviours stay pinned. Cost: one more parameter on a
function with six of them.

### 2026-08-18 — trust the broker on a ticker's first sync

**SUPERSEDED the same day — see "a board position larger than the
broker's is another platform's" below. Do not follow this entry.**

The alternative — treat any board excess as another platform's slice —
preserves whatever the board happened to be carrying with no way back,
and would have frozen both live errors (PLTR at 0 against 55 held, GOOG
at 24 against 22) permanently. What made the original overwrite
dangerous was that it also destroyed lots and sells; that part is not
repeated. Cost: a position genuinely split across brokers has to be
edited once after its first sync, after which the `t212Shares` tag
protects it.

### 2026-08-18 — one component, two views

The Investment panel is a `view` prop on `PerfChart`, not a sibling
component with its own data path. Sharing the drawing code is a bonus;
sharing the *pipeline* is the point, because that is what makes the two
panels structurally incapable of disagreeing.

### 2026-08-18 — a board position larger than the broker's is another platform's

**Supersedes "trust the broker on a ticker's first sync" above.** That
rule deleted 71 SPCX, 11.5 RKLB and 30 HOOD shares from a live book on
its first run, and the owner caught it by looking at the site. The
excess was never stale data; it was the rest of the position, and his
own records for the other platform match the deleted amounts to the
share.

The reasoning that justified the overwrite was wrong on its own terms
too: PLTR came back in full either way, because `max(0, 0 − 55)` is 0
and the broker's slice is the whole position when the board reads
sold-out. The rule bought nothing and cost three holdings.

So: on a ticker's first sync the board keeps `max(0, board − broker)`
and adds the broker's slice on top. Cost: a board that is genuinely
stale HIGH stays high until the owner edits it — which is a number he
can see and fix, unlike shares that vanish.

Rejected alternative: keeping the overwrite and adding a confirmation
step. A sync that runs on every refresh tick has no one to confirm with.

### 2026-08-18 — a skipped fill must not park the whole backfill

`ordersPageShapeMismatch` froze the cursor whenever one item on a page
carried a `fill` the shaper couldn't read, so that the walk could never
advance past a shape nobody had seen. In production the opposite
happened: two unreadable rows per page held both account cursors still
for the entire life of the feature — ISA stored nothing at all, invest
stopped a month back — and because the walk never latches `complete`,
the top-up pass that fetches TODAY's fills never ran either. Protecting
one row cost the whole history.

Now a page freezes only when NOTHING on it parsed, which is the signal
that the shaper rather than the row is at fault. A `fill` that isn't an
object at all still freezes unconditionally. Cost: a genuinely
unreadable row on an otherwise-good page is skipped silently rather than
stopping the world; the skip reason is still tallied into `last_error`.

### 2026-08-18 — broker fills are shown, not merged

**SUPERSEDED the next day — see "the ledger IS the broker's history"
below. Do not follow this entry.**

The lot editor lists Trading 212's fills for the ticker and marks which
ones the ledger already has, but folding them in takes a click. An
automatic merge would have to de-duplicate machine rows against
hand-typed ones on a book where 16 of 26 ledgers are incomplete, and
getting that wrong writes double lots into the YTD chart's input. Every
data loss on this repo has come from a sync deciding it knew better.
Cost: the ledger only catches up when the owner asks it to.

### 2026-08-19 — the ledger IS the broker's history

**Supersedes "broker fills are shown, not merged" above.** That design
assumed the two records correspond row for row. They don't: SPCX carried
one lot of `59 @ 144.31` — T212's reported AVERAGE, not a trade — against
twelve real fills running 165.58 down to 115.48. A 1:1 matcher calls all
twelve new, so the "add missing" button would have booked 118 shares
where 59 were held. The owner read the panel and couldn't tell what it
was claiming, which was the first symptom.

So a synced holding's ledger is rebuilt from the fills outright. The
caution that motivated the old entry is kept as two rules rather than as
a click: only a ticker with a `t212Shares` tag and fills to its name is
touched, and the result must net to the board's own share count or
nothing is written. `src: 'other'` protects what the broker can't see.

`cost` follows the rebuilt ledger too — the board's figure was T212's
buy-only average, which disagrees with this app's net-cash basis on any
holding that was sold. Eight of fourteen agree to the cent; ORCL differs
by $28.68/share. Put to the owner with the numbers; he chose the trades.

Cost: a holding the backfill hasn't reached keeps a ledger that looks
stale, and says so, until the walk gets there.


### 2026-08-19 — a PR branch is rebuilt on `main`, not merged with it

Merging `main` into PR #209 twice (`f58b11b`, `9db7e1d`) kept the diff
honest — a three-dot diff can't show anything already on `main` — but it
put `main`'s own commits into the PR's commit list, where they read as
nineteen commits of unreviewed work the PR was proposing. The owner read
it that way and asked for the landed content to be deleted.

Rebuilt as four commits straight on top of `main`, split by concern.
The tree was checked byte-identical to the old tip before the
force-push, so the committed bundle, the Cloudflare preview and the CI
outcome all carry over; only the history changed. The alternative —
leaving the merges and only rewriting the summary — was rejected
because the commit list is part of what a reviewer reads, and no wording
in the description makes nineteen commits look like four.

Cost: the per-commit history from the original build is gone, and the
four commits are split by file, so an intermediate one is not
independently green. Acceptable on a branch that merges as a unit; it
would not be on `main`.

### 2026-08-19 — the PR description is maintained like this file

`handover.md` was already required to be true in real time. The PR
description was not, and it drifted the moment work started landing on
`main` separately: by 2026-08-19 most of its length described the T212
backfill fix, the PLTR restore and migrations `0028`/`0030`–`0032`, all
of which had shipped. Someone reading it would have thought that work
was still up for review.

The rule now sits in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` under "Pull requests",
and in the working-with-davies skill: every push that changes the diff
rewrites the description in the same step, the description covers only
what the PR would add to `main` right now, and it carries the
Cloudflare preview link so the branch can be checked on a real machine.

The preview alias is derivable — branch name lowercased,
non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to `-`, truncated to 28 characters —
but it is derived and then **verified**, by fetching it and checking the
`assets/app-<hash>.js` it serves is the branch's committed bundle and
not `main`'s. Guessing the URL and quoting it unverified is the failure
mode this replaces.


### 2026-08-19 — a client change ships only after the server accepts it

A Cloudflare preview always talks to the PRODUCTION Edge Functions;
there is no preview backend. So a branch that starts sending a new
request header cannot be previewed at all until the deployed functions
allow that header — and worse, it looks like it works, because the
three callers involved all degrade quietly rather than erroring.

The rule taken from it: the CORS allow-list ships FIRST, on its own, in
a change that requires nothing; the client starts sending the header
second; enforcement lands last. Advertising a header nobody requires
costs nothing. Requiring one before it is advertised costs the release
— and, on a preview, costs the ability to check the release at all.

Rejected alternative: shipping both halves together on merge. It would
have worked for a fresh page load and broken every tab still holding
the previous bundle from its service worker, with the same silent
degradation instead of an error.

### 2026-08-19 — the heading is the view switch

The panel's two views were swapped by a `⇄` button beside the title.
It named neither destination and gave no state: the only feedback was
the title rewriting itself after the click. Replaced with two tabs at
panel-title scale — the active one in full chalk over a chalk
underline, the other dim behind a hairline — so the control says where
it goes and what you are looking at, in the space the title already
occupied. Roving tabindex and arrow keys, because a tablist that is a
heading still has to be reachable without a mouse.

The underline is a pseudo-element rather than a `border-bottom`: at
0.2em tracking the last glyph carries a trailing letter-space inside
its box, and the border ran under it, overshooting the final character
by about 2px.


### 2026-08-19 — a lagged NAV is not a mover

`017731` is a CN fund: its quote is a NAV published after its own close,
not a live price. `TOP MOVERS · TODAY` ranked it anyway for the whole
session — `cnSuppress` in `metrics.js` only zeroes it while the
extended-hours toggle is on — so a +9.9 % NAV print could top WINNERS
against stocks measured on today's tape. Two different questions in one
list.

Excluded from the ranking only. It still counts in the scoreboard and
still draws a heat-map tile: the number is real, it just isn't an answer
to "what moved today". The alternative — hiding it from the heat map too
— was rejected because the tile is about what the book holds, not about
today.


### 2026-08-26 — a source that cannot see the tape must record nothing

`snapshot-record` records what it can price. Its fallback order was
T212, then Yahoo's ext print, then Yahoo's last price — and the third
step is wrong overnight, because Yahoo has no overnight tape at all:
its quote is the last regular print, frozen until 04:00 ET. So a
missing T212 sample did not produce a gap, it produced a fabricated
bar, and because T212 is one fetch for the entire book it fabricated
the SAME kind of bar for all 21 US holdings at once. That is why it
showed up as the portfolio line tearing rather than one ticker
wobbling.

The rule taken from it: a price source that is asleep is not a fallback.
`recordablePrice` already said so about the board's stored `lastPrice`
("recording it would stamp a stale figure with a fresh timestamp") —
the mistake was not carrying that reasoning to Yahoo in a window where
Yahoo is equally asleep. Recording nothing leaves the chart on the
overnight recorder's own series, which is authoritative there anyway.

Rejected alternative: defending in the client, by having
`mergeRecordedBars` refuse recorded bars inside a span the overnight
recorder owns. It would have hidden the tearing without fixing the
stored data, and the stored data is what every later window reads.

Diagnosis note worth keeping: the offline reconstruction is what found
this. Running the repo's own `mergeOvernightSeries` / `buildTickerSeries`
/ `computeAt` over the REAL recorded points, REAL Yahoo bars and the
REAL share counts produced a smooth line — 0.308 pp as the largest step
across 272 points. The line being smooth in reconstruction while jagged
on screen is what proved the fault was in an input the reconstruction
had left out, and the only one left out was `price_snapshots`.

### [2026-09-17 22:55 UTC] Platform: Claude Code | Model: not recorded (session policy)

**1W is 15-minute bars.** Davies said 1W and 3M looked sparse beside the
other ranges, and the arithmetic agrees: at 60m a trailing week holds
about 35 points (7 bars a session x 5 sessions) against 1M's ~154. 15m
gives ~130. Yahoo serves 15m back 60 days, inside the month 1W already
fetches; the cost is roughly 3.7x the bars per ticker, which is why
every 1W cache TTL drops to 15 minutes in step.

Five places encode "how long is a 1W bar", for five different consumers,
and they were ALREADY out of step: `RANGES` said 60m while
`maFetchParamsFor` used 30m, so the MA overlay was computed over bars
the chart never drew and "MA20" covered twice the span it appeared to.
All five now say 15m — `RANGES`, `maFetchParamsFor`,
`NIGHT_BAR_INTERVAL_MS` (the recorded-overnight downsample, which has to
match or the splice changes resolution mid-night),
`ticker_chart_helpers.modalTtl` and `cache.RANGE_TTL_MS` — and a test
asserts they agree so the next change cannot drift one of them again.

cadence change has to be swept for every number DERIVED from the
cadence, not just for the places that restate it. Restating is easy to
grep; deriving is not.

**Merged, and production's ORIGIN is fixed — but the edge is still
serving five cached copies of the old exposure, and this session put
them there.**

After the merge, a plain fetch of production showed `/LEDGER.md`,
`/handover.md`, `/src/app.jsx`, `/package.json` and
`/supabase/functions/auth/index.ts` still returning their real
contents, while `/supabase/migrations/0029_price_snapshots.sql` —
requested for the first time in that same command — came back as the

between those paths is not what they are, it is that I had fetched the

Confirmed three ways: `cf-cache-status: HIT` with a climbing `age`;
the same five paths with a `?cb=` query string (a different cache key)
all return the shell; and six paths never fetched this session
— `/src/metrics.js`, `/supabase/functions/data/index.ts`, `/README.md`
and others — return the shell with no cache entry at all.

Nothing here can evict them. `*.pages.dev` is not a zone this account
can purge, a new deployment does not invalidate paths that are no
longer part of any deployment, and Cloudflare ignores `Cache-Control:
no-cache` and `Pragma: no-cache` from a client. They expire on their
own inside seven days.

**The lesson is not about Cloudflare.** Probing a resource to prove it
is exposed is itself a request, and on a CDN a request is a write. The
check extended the exposure it was measuring. Where the same check can
be made against a path nobody has touched — as `?cb=` or an unfetched
sibling does here — use that instead.

Scope, stated plainly: five paths, at whichever colo this container's
proxy egresses through, for up to a week. `auth/index.ts` was already
public for months, which is why rotating the secrets is the item above
it and not a new one.

produce bands that ran the full width.

So the layout is bands by construction. Each pass lays ONE band across
the full width (or full height) of the space left; the leftover is a
rectangle and the next band fills it the same way, so every seam runs
edge to edge inside its own region. Variety moved into the band: how many
holdings share it, hence its thickness and its tile widths. The count is
scored against a shape the band is asked for — tile width over band
thickness, 0.62 to 1.75 along a golden-ratio walk — so consecutive bands
never come out the same. On his book that is two, then three, then a
column of three.

**Two guards, and both were learned the hard way in this session.** A
count is refused if it puts a tile under the label size, past 3:1, OR
leaves a strip too thin for another band. That third one is the same
lesson as yesterday's veto-with-no-comparison, one level up: judging a
cut only by its own two halves and never by what it leaves behind is how
the CN fund ended in a 13 x 246 splinter. And the count that takes
everything remaining is NOT exempt from the guards — left competing on
score it won on the fixture's five-holding book and swept the lot into
one band. It reaches the layout only as the last-resort fallback.

The tail hands over to the ORIGINAL binary split, below 90 px of short
side or 6 holdings left: a band can only span the full width, so a 1 %
tail becomes a row of slivers, while a nested corner can still give the
same holdings squarish tiles. That corner is the part of the old board
he liked, kept as it was.

the messy version, which is the trade he asked for.

tape against −0.22 % / +20.62 % on Coinbase's — same sign, same order.
Swapping the entire price series moves the recommendation by about a
point. So WHAT TO RUN is robust and WHICH COIN DESERVES A SEAT is not,
which is the case for holding five of them, arrived at by accident. It
also means §4.15's bar is applied per coin per window, exactly where the
measurement is least stable. Not re-run: re-pricing the reference on
Kraken's tape is a study, not an edit, and it is now the top candidate
for the next one.

K1 is a firmer no than §3.12's: six slow rulebooks over 68 coins (622
online Kraken USD pairs measured keylessly, 199 clear $100k a day), and
in **952 coin-window cells Kraken beats the same rule at Revolut X's fees
exactly zero times**; 12 two-window passes against 16.28 by chance;
ZEC/XMR/TRX each clear one window and none two. K2 verdicts: delete
`trend-1h·revx`, `momentum-1d·kraken`, `rotation-1d·revx`,
`rotation-1w·kraken`; keep `momentum-1d·revx` unoptimised (the only row
not correlated with another) and `trend-4h·kraken` for its fill
measurement alone. K3: three candidates, all at chance on return.
**No migration written** — the third-window study is still running and
one migration should carry both verdicts.

### [2026-09-22 00:19 UTC] Platform: Claude Code | Model: not recorded (session policy)

**The maker question now has an instrument instead of an argument.**
Migration `0042` adds `agent_maker_probes`. Revolut X is 0 % maker and
the loop crosses the touch, so "rest everything and pay nothing" is the
standing question; §3.13 could not answer it because the backtest runs on
Coinbase candles with a synthetic bid and duly reports that a resting
order fills with a median delay of ZERO hours — the model's limit, not a
measurement. What it cannot see is the only thing that decides it: on a
breakout rule a resting bid fills exactly when the breakout fails, so the
fills you get are the bad half of the distribution.

The probe measures that on the real book at no cost and without resting
anything. Every marketable order writes down where a post-only order
would have sat (the same side's touch); turn 2b resolves it against the
execution venue's last closed minute — came back or not, and after how
many minutes — and then records the mark at +15 and +60. That last gap is
the adverse selection in bps, read against §3.13's 10–20 bps break-even
band. **A probe is never an order**: not in any position, book, exposure
or P&L; written last in `place()` so a probe that fails to insert cannot
cost an order; and it adds one public minute-candle call only on a symbol
the loop has just traded.

Two design notes worth keeping. The tick's read is a single
`watching=eq.true` over one partial index, NOT a compound predicate over
`state` and `follow_up` — the first version used PostgREST's `or=(…)`,
which the test stub rightly refused, and the simpler column is better
anyway. And the insert writes `state`, `watching` and `follow_up`
explicitly rather than leaning on column defaults: the starting state of
a probe is part of what the code means.

Pinned by `tick.test.ts`: `probeFilled`, `probeFollowUpDue`, and three
end-to-end cases (a marketable order opens a probe at the OTHER side's
touch and places nothing extra; a resting probe fills or expires against
the minute; a resolved probe collects m15 then m60 and stops being
watched). 320 passed / 0 failed.

**An independent audit found that there was no working way to stop a live
row that still held coins.** Three mechanisms, each independently broken,
each reproduced against the real code, and together they meant that on the
day a real position went wrong every lever the operator has been told to
pull either did nothing or made it worse.

1. **`live_confirmed_at = null` refused EXITS.** The check in `place()`
   tested the row's mode and the confirmation and never the SIDE, and it
   sits after `riskGate` has already allowed the exit. That switch is the
   first sentence of the emergency procedure in `go-live.md`. Pulling it
   would have left real coins with no floor and no rule exit, writing a
   decision row and an `ops_errors` row a minute per symbol while the
   record said the exit was allowed. Side-aware now; `global_pause` stays
   the one switch that outranks an exit.
2. **A paused row's exit order violated the schema, so the whole
   `windingDown` fix was INERT in production.** `agent_orders_mode_check`
   is `in ('paper','live')`; the tick wrote `mode: s.mode`, which is
   `'paused'` for exactly the rows `0038` and `0043` retired. The decision
   landed (no check on that table), the ORDER was refused by Postgres, the
   error carried no `409|duplicate|unique` so it was swallowed into
   `report.errors`, and the page went on telling the owner the floor was
   running. **My own tests certified it**, because the in-memory stub does
   not enforce CHECK constraints. The stub enforces the mode check now, and
   reverting the fix turns those three tests red.
3. **A live row demoted to `mode = 'paper'` read itself flat** — offered
   as an undo — so its real coins lost their exits while it started buying
   on paper beside them.

One root: **a row's `mode` LABEL and the book it is trading are different
things.** `bookMode(s, sym)` resolves the book — real coins outrank the
label, else the row's mode, a paused row falling back to paper — and the
order, the decision, the probe, the exposure bucket and the caps all follow
the BOOK. `riskGate` keeps the LABEL, because "may this rulebook take new
risk" is what it asks. `offBook()` generalises `windingDown` from "retired"
to "holds a book it does not trade".

**Two more holes left a real position unprotected.** An order that could
not be read back or cancelled blocked its pair's stop every minute,
indefinitely — and an unreadable filled order is exactly what B4 produces
if the settlement field names are wrong, so the first live order could both
fail to settle AND disarm the stop on the coin it just bought. A `pending`
row, which is what a venue timeout produces, did the same. A buy is not the
exit: the stop steps past it, says so, and sells what is held; only a SELL
in flight still stands it down.

**The dashboard had not been given this morning's fix** — `index.ts` still
keyed on strategy and symbol with no mode and billed `byMode` from the row's
label, so a row that ever changed mode drew one position out of two books
and the whole blend landed under "live realised". It resolves the book the
same way the tick does now.

Four smaller fixes: a `filled` reply reporting `filled_size: 0` is a problem
rather than a fill of the whole order at fee zero (absent is still absent —
that distinction cost a test); `positionFromFills` sorts to a total order,
buy-first at a tie; `stepDecimals` reads an exponential step; a paused row is
refused before `askJev` is paid. **`0045` makes `agent_maker_probes`
cascade** — a THIRD child of `agent_strategies` that `0044` did not delete,
which survived on luck because the only three probe rows belonged to a row
that stayed. Orders and decisions stay explicit: a forgotten one should fail
loudly, which is what happened.

### [2026-09-22 18:33 UTC] Platform: Claude Code | Model: not recorded (session policy)

**The real model was asked about every state it can ever see on an
entry, five times each, and the Jev question is answered.** The entry
state has only 90 possible values (5 coins × trend_strength ×
volatility × momentum; the rest is fixed on an entry). `POST
?action=jev` asked OpenRouter's `typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917` all 90 ×
5 = 450 calls, $0.0126, requests 26655/26656, zero no-answers, zero echo
failures:

| strength | vol | momentum | P(healthy) mean [min–max] | vetoed at 0.6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weak | any | positive | 0.07–0.13 | **100 %** |
| moderate/strong | low/normal | positive | 0.94–0.97 | 0 % |
| moderate | high | positive | **0.600** [0.55–0.62] | 7/25 |
| strong | high | positive | **0.598** [0.56–0.64] | 12/25 |
| any | any | unknown | 0.04–0.21 | 100 % |

Caution never reaches 1.75 on an entry. **Two findings, both
structural:** (1) **the weak-trend veto is not the model's judgment — it
is the question's own prose**: `healthy_trend` tells the model to say yes
only when trend_strength is moderate or strong, the rulebook never reads
strength, and the model complies every time. That clause is an
untested rule hiding in a prompt, and it is what costs the bear year most
of its return in the earlier study (`weak-veto-only`: A +8.03 % → +0.63 %).
(2) **the high-volatility veto is a coin flip AT the threshold**: those
states' mean P sits on 0.600, and the same state on the same coin flips
between calls (strong|high ETH: 0.58 0.58 0.61 0.63 0.64). Whether real
money buys a high-volatility breakout would be decided by one call's
noise. The earlier study's bracket (`highvol-vetoed` / `highvol-passed`)
is therefore the honest answer and its "central" arm is not; its
assumed 0.15 for the weak states is confirmed (measured 0.07–0.13).

**Re-pricing with these answers is running** (Monte Carlo over the
coin-flip states; three configurations — rule with the model in shadow,
rule ∧ model as it runs, rule + the weak-trend clause as code — each
against its random-veto null). Nothing about the live row changes until
it lands and is checked. `docs/agents/backtests/jev_answers.json` will
hold the raw replies; `net._http_response` prunes them after ~6 h, and
re-measuring costs $0.013.

**A shadow switch, built and NOT switched on.** `params.jevGate: false`
on a strategy row keeps asking the model and recording its answer but
takes away its vote: the entry is the rulebook's — what every backtest
prices — and the decision's reason says what the gate WOULD have done
("model in shadow — would veto (P=0.59 < 0.6)"), so the counterfactual
stays one query away. Two of the three configurations the go-live
decision is choosing between need it; the default keeps today's
behaviour on every row, so nothing in production changes. Pinned in
`strategy.test.ts` and `tick.test.ts`; counterfactual checked (ignore the
switch in the tick and the new test fails).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - React 18 automatic batching / state-update timing: `setState` inside a Promise `.then()` does NOT apply synchronously; downstream refs/callbacks that depend on the NEW state must wait for a subsequent render+commit+effect cycle.
   - React effect ordering within a single commit: effects run in DECLARATION ORDER (top-to-bottom in source) for the same commit — used to sequence a `doRefreshRef.current = doRefresh` sync effect before a NEW effect that reads `doRefreshRef.current`.
   - `useRef`'s lazy-initial-value pattern: `useRef(expr)` only evaluates `expr` on the FIRST render; used to capture "was there cache data at mount" once (`hadCachedPortfolioRef`).
   - React state-updater purity: mutating a ref inside a `setState(prev => ...)` functional updater is an anti-pattern (impure, could double-fire under StrictMode) — this realization is driving the REDESIGN of the P1 fix.
   - Optimistic concurrency / If-Match versioning: `portfolio_remote.js`'s `lastKnownVersion` module-scope variable, sent as `If-Match` header on save; if `null`, the save is UNCONDITIONAL (no conflict check) — this is the crux of the P1 data-loss risk.
   - Parallel-race fetch pattern (Promise executor + `resolved`/`remaining`/`controllers`/`timers`/`cleanup()`/`settle()`) — used in both `historical.js` (pre-existing) and now `yahoo_fetch.js` (new, mirrors it) for CORS-proxy fallback racing.
   - AbortController/AbortSignal semantics: aborting a controller mid-fetch causes the fetch promise to reject with an AbortError; this lands in generic `catch` blocks indistinguishable from genuine network/timeout errors UNLESS explicitly disambiguated (the P2 bug/fix).
   - Supabase Edge Functions (Deno Deploy) cold starts: no documented min-instances/keep-warm config; mitigated via a scheduled GitHub Actions ping (`healthcheck.yml`).
   - `verifyToken` gating order in Edge Functions (`data`/`trading212`): auth check runs BEFORE any upstream/DB call, so anonymous pings expecting 401 are safe (prove isolate booted, no side effects).
   - localStorage `dp.*` namespace pattern (`storage.js`) — `Storage.loadXCache()`/`saveXCache()` pairs, `{ts, data}` shape, staleness caps, demo-row rejection guards.
   - Vitest testing patterns: `vi.mock()` module mocking, `vi.mocked(fn).mockReturnValueOnce(new Promise(...))` for manually-controlled async timing in tests, `waitFor()` from `@testing-library/react`.
   - GitHub PR review workflow: Codex bot (`chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`) leaves both a top-level "About Codex" boilerplate comment AND separate threaded review comments (retrieved via `mcp__github__pull_request_read` method `get_review_comments`, NOT visible in the top-level comment body) with P1/P2 severity badges.
   - CLAUDE.md git workflow: PR (not direct push) required for "cross-cutting refactor" changes; Codex review must be addressed before merge; commits authored as `daviesluo <daviesluo@gmail.com>`, never as Claude.

1	// Public CORS proxy chain + per-proxy backoff cache.
2	//
3	// The Edge Function /functions/v1/prices does the bulk of Yahoo
4	// fetching server-side, but a CORS-proxy fallback exists for:
5	//   - cold Edge deploys / outages,
6	//   - CN funds where Deno Deploy's egress IPs sometimes get
7	//     geo-blocked from eastmoney / pingzhongdata.
8	// All 5 hosts are free public proxies with aggressive per-IP rate
9	// limits; without the backoff cache, one bad proxy poisons every
10	// 30s refresh until the user reloads.
11	
12	export const PROXIES = [
13	  (url) => `https://api.cors.lol/?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`,
14	  (url) => `https://corsproxy.io/?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`,
15	  (url) => `https://api.allorigins.win/raw?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`,
16	  (url) => `https://api.codetabs.com/v1/proxy?quest=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`,
17	  (url) => `https://cors.eu.org/${url}`,
18	];
19	
20	// Per-proxy backoff cache. When a proxy returns 429 / 403 / 5xx (or
21	// times out) we mark it "dead" for `PROXY_BACKOFF_MS` so the next
22	// 30-second refresh tick skips it instead of immediately re-hammering
23	// the same broken host. Cleared on success and on natural expiry.
24	//
25	// In-memory only — resets on page reload (intentional; proxies recover
26	// over time and we'd rather re-probe a fresh tab than carry a 10-min
27	// suspicion across sessions).
28	export const PROXY_BACKOFF_MS = 10 * 60_000;
29	const _proxyBackoff = new Map(); // index → expire-at ms
30	
31	export function proxyIsAvailable(i, now = Date.now()) {
32	  const t = _proxyBackoff.get(i);
33	  if (t == null) return true;
34	  if (t > now) return false;
35	  _proxyBackoff.delete(i);   // expired — clear and let it back in
36	  return true;
37	}
38	export function markProxyDead(i, durationMs = PROXY_BACKOFF_MS) {
39	  _proxyBackoff.set(i, Date.now() + durationMs);
40	}
41	export function clearProxyBackoff(i) {
42	  if (i == null) _proxyBackoff.clear();
43	  else _proxyBackoff.delete(i);
44	}
45

### assistant  ·  2026-07-20 17:42:03

两个 Codex 发现的问题已经修复并推送到 PR #201（commit `aa9eb17`）：

**P1（app.jsx，数据丢失风险）**：之前逻辑是不管加载成功与否，先无条件把 `hasRealLoadRef.current` 设为 `true` 打开保存门。修复后：如果真实加载失败/返回空账户（`_isDemo`）、且屏幕上已经是缓存的真实数据，则直接提前 return，**不**打开保存门——避免这次失败的加载在未确认 `lastKnownVersion` 的情况下，让后续编辑跳过 `If-Match` 无条件覆盖服务器上其他设备写入的新数据。

**P2（yahoo_fetch.js + historical.js，代理误拉黑）**：并行赛跑多个 CORS 代理时，赢家的 `cleanup()` 会 abort 所有陪跑请求，这些 abort 之前被当成真超时一样拉黑 60 秒——健康的代理只是慢了半拍就被误伤。修复后在 catch 块里加了 `if (resolved) return;` 判断，只有真正超时/网络错误才拉黑。同样的 bug 也存在于 `historical.js`（我抄它的模式带过去的），一并修了。

已加了对应的回归测试（3个新用例），四项本地检查（typecheck / lint / test / build）全部通过，567 个测试全绿。CI（`typecheck-and-build`）目前还在跑，Cloudflare Pages 预览已经部署成功。我会继续按订阅盯着这个 PR，CI 出结果或 Codex 有新反馈会再同步。

Each ticker's\n// fallback races ALL proxies at once, so an unbounded `missing.map(...)`\n// over a 30-ticker portfolio fires 30 × 5 = 150 simultaneous fetches\n// the moment the Edge Function is down — enough for Chromium to start\n// rejecting them outright with net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES, turning\n// a degraded refresh into a totally failed one. 6 tickers at a time\n// (≤30 in-flight fetches) keeps the fallback fast without the pile-up.\nexport async function mapWithConcurrency(items, limit, fn) {\n  const out = new Array(items.length);\n  let next = 0;\n  const worker = async () => {\n    while (next < items.length) {\n      const i = next++;\n      out[i] = await fn(items[i], i);\n    }\n  };\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, items.length) }, worker));\n  return out;\n}",

43	export function localMinOfDay(utcSec: number, gmtOffsetSec: number): number {

Deno.test("cryptoUsSessionQuote: US HOLIDAY during RTH clock → off-session (extPrice=live, lastPrice=last REAL close)", () => {
  // Fri 2026-07-03 is the observed Independence Day holiday. The clock reads
  // 13:45 ET (inside 9:30-16:00) but the market is closed all day, so the
  // 24/7 crypto is off-session: its live price must land in extPrice and
  // lastPrice must be the last REAL trading-day close (Thu 07-02), NOT the
  // holiday's own mid-day candle. This is the "BTC shows 0.00% on July 3" bug.
  const rows: Array<[string, number]> = [
    ["2026-07-01T16:00:00-04:00", 100],  // Wed close ← prev
    ["2026-07-02T16:00:00-04:00", 110],  // Thu close ← last (last real close)
    ["2026-07-03T11:00:00-04:00", 120],  // Fri HOLIDAY mid-day — must be skipped
    ["2026-07-03T13:45:00-04:00", 125],  // Fri HOLIDAY mid-day — must be skipped
  ];
  const ts = rows.map((r) => tsOf(r[0]));
  const cl = rows.map((r) => r[1]);
  const nowSec = tsOf("2026-07-03T13:45:00-04:00");
  const q = cryptoUsSessionQuote(ts, cl, /*live*/ 125, /*prevMeta*/ 40, nowSec, EDT);
  // lastPrice = Thu close (110), extPrice = live (125), prevClose = Wed close (100).
  // Client shows (125-110)/110 ≈ +13.6% "since the last close" instead of 0%.
  assertEquals(q, { lastPrice: 110, extPrice: 125, prevClose: 100 });
});

{
  "content": "// Pins mapWithConcurrency — the bounded fan-out used by the per-ticker\n// proxy fallbacks. Each ticker's fallback races all 5 proxies at once,\n// so an unbounded map over a 30-ticker portfolio fired ~150 fetches the\n// moment the Edge Function was down — enough for Chromium to reject\n// them with net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES and turn a degraded refresh\n// into a totally failed one (observed in the 2026-07 cold-start\n// investigation's browser reproduction).\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';\nimport { mapWithConcurrency } from './proxy_chain.js';\n\ndescribe('mapWithConcurrency', () => {\n  it('never runs more than `limit` callbacks at once', async () => {\n    let inFlight = 0;\n    let peak = 0;\n    const items = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => i);\n    const out = await mapWithConcurrency(items, 6, async (n) => {\n      inFlight++;\n      peak = Math.max(peak, inFlight);\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5));\n      inFlight--;\n      return n * 2;\n    });\n    expect(peak).toBeLessThanOrEqual(6);\n    expect(peak).toBeGreaterThan(1); // it IS still concurrent\n    expect(out).toEqual(items.map((n) => n * 2));\n  });\n\n  it('preserves input order in the results regardless of completion order', async () => {\n    const out = await mapWithConcurrency([30, 5, 20], 3, async (ms) => {\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n      return ms;\n    });\n    expect(out).toEqual([30, 5, 20]);\n  });\n\n  it('handles empty input and limit larger than the item count', async () => {\n    expect(await mapWithConcurrency([], 6, async () => 1)).toEqual([]);\n    expect(await mapWithConcurrency([1, 2], 10, async (n) => n)).toEqual([1, 2]);\n  });\n});\n",

### assistant  ·  2026-07-20 18:24:22

这次找到真正的根源了,而且是拿实锤证据修的。**PR #202**:https://github.com/daviesluo/daviesportfolios/pull/202

## 根源:017731(中国基金)

从 Supabase 日志看你 17:48 那次测试:**每一次 `prices` 请求都只返回 29/30 只票——017731 永远缺失**(其他票全部 200、最慢 2.3 秒)。链条是:

1. Edge Function 取 CN 基金只靠 eastmoney 的 fundgz 接口,而 Deno 服务器的出口 IP 被它地域封锁 → 每次响应都悄悄缺了这只基金
2. 客户端发现缺票 → 走代理兜底,但那是个**串行**循环:5 个免费 CORS 代理逐个试、每个 8 秒超时,而西方代理基本连不上 eastmoney → **整个刷新等着它干耗 ~20-40 秒**
3. **页内刷新快**:失败代理已进内存黑名单,循环直接跳过 → 只剩 2-3 秒的 Edge 请求
4. **关掉重开又慢**:黑名单是内存的,重开就清零 → 再跑一遍串行超时

我用无头浏览器做了 A/B 对照:同样模拟条件下,**旧版 bundle spinner 40.7 秒,修复后 0.6 秒**。

## 修了什么

- **服务端根治**:`prices` 函数的 CN 基金路径加了 lsjz / danjuanapp 兜底(fundgz 和 lsjz 并发跑,取最近两天官方净值)——lsjz 实测通,017731 不会再缺席
- **客户端免疫**:就算再缺票,代理兜底也**完全不阻塞刷新**——立即返回拿到的 29 只,兜底转后台,结果缓存并在下个 tick 合并
- **顺手修掉**:Edge 全挂时 30 票 × 5 代理 = 150 并发请求把浏览器打崩的问题(限 6 票一波),以及波与波之间重复硬闯已拉黑代理的叠加超时

Deno's test sanitizer\n  // rightly flags either as a leak.\n  let settled = false;\n  let graceTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n  const preempt: Promise<PriceResult | typeof PENDING> = lsjzPromise.then(async (ls) => {\n    if (!ls || settled) return PENDING;   // useless lsjz never preempts fundgz\n    await new Promise<void>((r) => { graceTimer = setTimeout(r, graceMs); });\n    return ls;\n  });\n  try {\n    const first = await Promise.race([gzPromise, preempt]);\n    if (first === PENDING) return await gzPromise; // lsjz was useless; fundgz gets its full timeout\n    if (first) return first;                       // usable fundgz, or lsjz preempting a hung fundgz\n    return await lsjzPromise;                      // fundgz settled null → fall back to lsjz\n  } finally {\n    settled = true;\n    if (graceTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(graceTimer);\n  }\n}",

### assistant  ·  2026-07-21 04:59:03

查清楚了，确实是预加载逻辑的 bug——而且能从截图精确对上。下面是完整诊断。

## 为什么全是 0.00%

左边 MC 卡片在扩展时段（ext）下算涨跌，用的锚点是 **`todayRegularClose`**（今天 16:00 ET 那根收盘 bar）。看 `header_sidebar.jsx:641-651` 的逻辑：ext 模式下如果 `todayRegularClose` 存在就用它当锚点，**不存在就回退成 `lastPrice`**。而卡片显示的 `price` 在夜盘对指数/FX 来说也是 `lastPrice`（期货的 `extPrice` 夜盘通常是 null，同样回退到 `lastPrice`）。于是：

```
涨跌% = (price − anchor) / anchor = (lastPrice − lastPrice) / lastPrice = 0.00%
```

关键佐证：如果只是数据没到，回退分支会退到 `d.dayPct`（常规日内涨跌，非零）。但你截图里是**精确的 0.00 / +0.00**，说明 `price` 和 `anchor` 都有值且相等——正是"锚点塌回 lastPrice"这条路径，13 张卡全中。

## 为什么"过了好久才有数字"

`todayRegularClose` 只在这个条件下才拉（`app.jsx:607`）：

```js
const wantTodayCloses = extendedHours && (Date.now() - todayClosesRef.current.ts > 30*60*1000);
```

它 gate 在 **`extendedHours` 开关本身**上。但是：
1. 冷启动时 ext 默认是**关**的（`useState(false)`，不持久化），所以首刷不会拉 `todayRegularClose`；
2. 你手动打开开关**不会触发刷新**（`app.jsx:929` 刷新循环只依赖 `[portfolio !== null]`，这是刻意设计的"切开关不重新拉数据"）。

所以打开开关的一刹那锚点还是空的 → 全 0；要**等下一次 30 秒自动刷新 tick**，`doRefresh` 才看到 `extendedHours=true`、才去拉 `fetchTodayRegularClose`（15 个 MC 符号的 5d/5m bar，本身还要一两秒），卡片才终于有数。这就是那段"过了好久"。

## 这是不一致导致的 bug

对比同一个 `doRefresh` 里持仓的夜盘预加载（`app.jsx:580`）：

```js
const wantsExtSeries = refreshPhase !== "regular";   // 按“时段”预加载，不管开关
```

持仓的夜盘 line / ext 判定是**"只要在非常规时段就预加载，无视开关"**——所以你切开关时它们是即时的。唯独 MC 卡片的锚点漏了这个待遇，按开关拉而不是按时段拉。代码注释里其实写着设计意图就是"预加载好，让切开关即时"，MC 锚点这行没跟上。

## 建议的修复（一行）

把 `app.jsx:607` 的 gate 从开关改成时段，和 `wantsExtSeries` 对齐：

```js
const wantTodayCloses = refreshPhase !== "regular"
  && (Date.now() - todayClosesRef.current.ts > 30 * 60 * 1000);
```

这样夜盘/盘前盘后**无论开关开没开**，首刷就会把 `todayRegularClose` 预拉好（30 分钟节流 + 在 `Promise.all` 里并行，成本很小，且只在非常规时段发生），你再打开 ext 开关就即时有数。对刚修好的冷启动几乎无影响（多一个 ~200ms 的并行调用，还带 30 分钟节流）。

要我直接改吗？改完我会跑一遍四项检查，并补一个 pin 测试锁住"夜盘预加载不 gate 在开关上"这个行为，再开 PR。

## 已修复并上线（commit `c8a7b7c`，main 的 `typecheck-and-build` ✅）

**改动**：把 `app.jsx` 里 MC 锚点预加载的 gate 从"开关"改成"时段"——

```js
// 改前：只有 ext 开关已经打开时才拉
const wantTodayCloses = extendedHours && (...30分钟节流...)
// 改后：只要在非常规时段就预拉，无视开关（和上一行持仓预加载 wantsExtSeries 对齐）
const wantTodayCloses = refreshPhase !== "regular" && (...30分钟节流...)
```

这样夜盘/盘前盘后每次刷新都会把 `todayRegularClose`（16:00 ET 收盘锚点）预热好，你再打开 ext 开关，13 张卡立刻显示真实涨跌，不再是"先全 0、等下一个 30 秒 tick 才有数"。

**成本没变**：依然 30 分钟节流、依然只在非常规时段拉、依然在 `Promise.all` 里并行——之前那个把 Supabase 带宽打爆的 egress 泄漏（每 30 秒重拉）不会回来。

**验证**：
- 加了 pin 测试锁住"夜盘预加载不 gate 在开关上"，并**实测过**——把 gate 改回旧写法测试就超时失败，改回新写法就过，证明测试真的守得住这个行为
- 四项检查全绿（typecheck / lint / 573 个测试 / build）
- README 两处同步（Highlights 段 + 文件表 `historical.js` 行）

**你这边怎么拿到**：这是纯前端改动，服务端没动。你的 PWA 会在接下来一两次打开时由 Service Worker 自动换上新 bundle，之后夜盘打开 ext 开关就即时有数了。可以晚点夜盘时再试一次确认。

改好推 main 了（commit `02149c4`），CI 在跑（本地四项全绿，和 CI 跑的是同一套）。

## 改动

给 treemap 加了"恰好 3 格"的特例：这类区域不再走通用二分（那个会切成"两个并排 + 一条整宽"，两个并排一大一小就显得别扭），改成**沿区域长边切三条等比例条带**：

- **竖高/接近正方的区域**（你截图那种）→ 三条**整宽横条，上/中/下叠放**，高度按市值，大的在上（MU → NET → 017731）。这就是你要的"上中下横着放"。
- **很宽扁的区域** → 切成三列整高条带。这么处理是为了避免在宽区域里硬横放变成又扁又读不了字的细条——那种情况下三列每个都是满高、标签放得下。

如果你想要**不管什么形状都强制横条**（包括宽区域也上中下），跟我说，我把长边判断去掉就行。

## 验证

- `treemap` 已导出，`heatmap.test.js` 加了 4 个用例把坐标钉死：竖高区域 → 三条整宽横条（x 全 0、宽全满、y=[0,180,270]、高按比例、末条精确填满无缝隙）；宽区域 → 三列；正方 → 横条；1/2 格布局不受影响。render 只是把 `tile.x/y/w/h` 原样映射到 div，所以单测坐标就是最终布局。
- typecheck / lint / 577 个测试 / build 全绿，README 的 `heatmap.jsx` 行也同步了。

纯前端改动，服务端没动。等 Cloudflare 部署完 + 你的 PWA 换上新 bundle，热力图里这种三格就是上中下三条横放了。夜盘或平时打开热力图看一眼即可，有不满意的形状再截图给我调。

## 问题出在我上次的改动

上次为了修"三格竖着放"，我给宽区域也切了**三列**——NVTS 值大占宽列，另外两个值小就成了你截图里那两条细长条。是我引入的回归，抱歉。

## 现在的规则

3 格区域按形状分两种，都不会出现细条：

- **竖高/正方区域** → 三条整宽横条，上/中/下（你第一个需求，保持不变）
- **宽区域** → 最大的占**满高度的左列**，另外两个在**右列上下叠放**（就是你要的"上下两个小长方块"）

另外加了防塌陷夹逼：左列宽度限制在 **40–70%**，右列上下分割限制在 **30–70%**。这样无论是 NVTS 那种一家独大，还是三个差不多大，任何一块都不会被挤成细条。

## 验证

- 9 个热力图布局测试（新增 2 个）把坐标钉死，其中一个专门用 NVTS 那种"一块占 85% 价值"的数据，断言右列宽度 ≥30%、上下两块高度都 ≥30%
- 拿你实际的 27 只票量级分布跑了模拟：4 种画布形状下**没有任何一块长宽比 ≥4:1**（最差 3.8:1，是正常矩形；截图里那两条约 7:1）。同时确认 3 格分支在真实布局里确实会命中 5 次、其中 2 次是宽区域——说明这个修复真的作用在你看到的那种格子上
- typecheck / lint / 578 个测试 / build 全绿，README 同步

CI 我挂了个后台任务在等结果，完成会通知我。等 Cloudflare 部署 + PWA 换新 bundle 后你再看看热力图，还有别扭的形状继续截图给我。

## 诊断结论

先说清楚:**服务端数据是好的,代码逻辑也是对的**——这两点我都实测过:

- 用你截图里那 26 只票查线上 `prices`:22 只美股 `extPrice` **全部正常**(只有 `2DG.F` 和 `017731` 是 null,这是按设计跳过的)
- 21 只票的盘前 K 线批量请求:21/21 都有盘前 bar
- 把这些真实数据灌进当前线上代码的完整管线跑:`extPriceTrusted` 全 true,dayPct 全部非零(NVDA −0.10%、AAPL +0.90% 等)

所以问题出在**你手机拿到的数据是旧的**。

## 根因:Service Worker 把旧行情当实时数据发

`vite.config.js` 里把 Supabase 实时行情接口也纳入了 `data-api` 缓存,配置是 **6 秒网络超时 + 6 小时有效期**。NetworkFirst 的机制是:网络只要慢过 6 秒,就直接拿缓存顶上。而 app 会把这个响应当成一次**成功刷新**——盖上 "Last updated"、pill 继续显示 LIVE。所以最多 6 小时前的行情会被当成实时数据展示,**连 STALE 提示都被绕过了**(这就是为什么你看到"LIVE / 6 秒前更新"却全是 0)。

为什么偏偏是美股全 0、BTC 和 SIVE 正常:陈旧的 ext 报价过不了 `extPriceIsRealAh` 的校验,而 `metrics.js` 里美股在 ext 分支下校验失败就**强制归 0**;BTC(加密)和 SIVE(欧股)根本不走 ext 分支,所以照常显示。

## 改动

把有效期从 6 小时压到 **5 分钟**(约一个刷新周期),超时从 6 秒提到 **10 秒**(低于 app 自己 8–12 秒的 fetch 超时,慢请求现在会真的等到结果,而不是被缓存抢先)。离线显示不受影响——那是走 app 自己的缓存(`dp.marketCache` / `dp.portfolioCache` / IndexedDB 图表库),那些有正常的陈旧/错误提示。

四项检查全绿(573 测试),README 已同步。

## 你这边

新 SW 部署后会接管,旧的 6 小时缓存条目按新规则很快失效。**如果现在还是全 0,在 app 里点一下版本更新横幅的 RELOAD**(或强制刷新)即可立刻切到新 SW。之后盘前再看,美股应该显示真实涨跌了。

需要说明的是:我没能直接抓到你手机当时的网络请求,所以"慢网触发缓存兜底"这一步是**推断**——但它是唯一能同时解释全部现象的机制,而且"把 6 小时前的行情标成 LIVE"这件事本身就是缺陷,无论是不是这次的直接原因都该修。如果换新版后还复现,告诉我,我再从别的方向查。

async function fetchYahoo(tickers) {
  const liveTickers = tickers.filter(t => !t.endsWith(".PVT") && t !== "CASH");
  if (!liveTickers.length) return {};

  // 6-digit numeric tickers are Chinese mutual funds.
  const cnFunds = liveTickers.filter(t => /^\d{6}$/.test(t));
  const hasCNFund = cnFunds.length > 0;
  if (hasCNFund) {
    // Edge Function first — it covers CN funds (fundgz with lsjz /
    // danjuanapp fallbacks server-side) so the happy path needs zero
    // CORS-proxy traffic. When the Edge response still omits a CN fund
    // (every server upstream failed), the proxy fallback runs in the
    // BACKGROUND: the refresh returns the fresh quotes it has right
    // away and the fund's quote (if a proxy ever gets one) is cached
    // and merged into the next tick. Awaiting the proxies here is what
    // used to stall the whole first refresh ~20 s — one geo-blocked
    // fund held 29 live quotes and the spinner hostage, on every cold
    // open (the in-memory proxy backoff resets per page load, so only
    // in-page refreshes were fast).
    const edgeResult = normalizeEdgeResult(await fetchViaEdge(liveTickers));
    if (edgeResult && cnFunds.every(t => edgeResult[t])) return edgeResult;
    const missingCn = cnFunds.filter(t => !edgeResult?.[t]);
    const out = { ...(edgeResult || {}) };
    for (const t of missingCn) {
      const cached = cnFundQuoteCache.get(t);
      if (cached && Date.now() - cached.ts < CN_FUND_QUOTE_TTL_MS) out[t] = cached.quote;
      refreshCNFundInBackground(t);
    }
    return Object.keys(out).length > 0 ? out : null;
  }

  // Edge Function first — it batches all tickers in one server-side
  // request and is the source of truth when healthy. Only fall back to
  // the per-ticker CORS-proxy chain for tickers the Edge missed; the
  // proxies have aggressive rate limits so racing them on every refresh
  // (the previous Promise.any approach) burned through their daily
  // quota even when the Edge Function was working fine.
  const edgeResult = await fetchViaEdge(liveTickers).then(normalizeEdgeResult).catch(() => null);
  const haveEverything = edgeResult && liveTickers.every(t => edgeResult[t]);
  if (haveEverything) return edgeResult;
  // Partial Edge response — narrow the proxy retry to JUST the tickers
  // Edge omitted, instead of either trusting the omissions (the old
  // policy, which produced the recurring "FX MISSING" pill the user
  // hit whenever Yahoo dropped GBPUSD=X for a single tick) or
  // re-fetching everything via proxy (which would shred the proxy
  // chain's rate limits). The proxies hit the same Yahoo upstream so
  // a non-transient miss still won't recover, but Yahoo's per-ticker
  // drops are mostly transient (the next refresh tick already has
  // them back) and a quick retry catches them before the silent 1:1
  // USD fallback in fxRateToUSD propagates into the portfolio total.
  const missing = edgeResult

  "old_string": "export async function refreshPrices(portfolio) {\n  const tickers = Object.keys(portfolio.holdings);\n  const result = await fetchYahoo(tickers);\n  if (!result || Object.keys(result).length === 0) {\n    return { updates: {}, source: \"error\" };\n  }\n  return { updates: result, source: \"live\" };\n}",
  "new_string": "// A tick that came back with only a fraction of the requested quotes is\n// an outage, not a live refresh. Below this share of the requested\n// tickers we report `error` so the header pill shows the failure and\n// the caller's 3 s retry kicks in.\nconst LIVE_COVERAGE_MIN = 0.5;\n\nexport async function refreshPrices(portfolio) {\n  const tickers = Object.keys(portfolio.holdings);\n  const result = await fetchYahoo(tickers);\n  if (!result || Object.keys(result).length === 0) {\n    return { updates: {}, source: \"error\" };\n  }\n  // Tickers fetchYahoo actually tries — the same filter it applies\n  // internally, so cash / `.PVT` placeholders don't count as misses.\n  const wanted = tickers.filter(\n    (t) => !t.endsWith(\".PVT\") && t !== \"CASH\" && !portfolio.holdings[t]?.isCash,\n  );\n  const got = wanted.filter((t) => result[t]).length;\n  // Why this exists: with a CN fund in the book, a totally unreachable\n  // Edge Function still produced a \"successful\" tick — the fund's\n  // background proxy cache supplied ONE quote, `fetchYahoo` returned\n  // that single-entry object, and the board went LIVE / \"Last updated\n  // 2 s\" while all 25 other holdings silently kept their previous\n  // values. The prices looked frozen but nothing surfaced the outage.\n  if (wanted.length > 0 && got / wanted.length < LIVE_COVERAGE_MIN) {\n    return { updates: result, source: \"error\" };\n  }\n  return { updates: result, source: \"live\" };\n}"
}

### assistant  ·  2026-08-06 10:31:44

已推 main（`17b92db`）。这次找到真凶了——上一次的缓存修复方向是错的，抱歉。

## 真正的原因（两个叠加的缺陷）

**1. Yahoo 已经不再返回 `preMarketPrice` / `postMarketPrice` 了**

代理兜底路径取盘前价的写法是 `meta.preMarketPrice ?? meta.postMarketPrice ?? null`。我实测了各种 interval/range 组合——**这两个字段全都不存在了**，所以恒为 null。而 `metrics.js` 里美股在 ext 模式下拿不到 extPrice 就**强制归 0**。于是只要走了代理兜底，整个美股板块就全部塌成 +0.00%，而 BTC（加密）和 SIVE（欧股）不走 ext 分支，照常显示——完全对应你两张截图。

顺带查出来一个更早就存在的错误：那个请求用的是 `interval=1d&range=5d`，它连 `previousClose` 都没有，代码只能退到 `chartPreviousClose`——**那是 5 天前的收盘价**（NVDA 195.04，正确应是 211.94）。所以代理兜底时的日涨跌一直是"多日涨跌"。

改成 `interval=5m&range=1d&includePrePost=true` 后两个问题一起解决：从 K 线里回扫最近一根非交易时段的 bar 取 extPrice（和 Edge 服务端同一套规则），`previousClose` 也正确了。**实测验证**：把 Edge 打挂后，AAPL 拿到 ext=313.99 → +0.96%，GOOG → +0.57%，不再是 0.00%。

**2. 故障被伪装成 LIVE**

这解释了为什么你的数据"冻结却显示 LIVE / 2 秒前更新"：因为你持有 017731，Edge 一旦不可达，CN 基金分支会用后台缓存的那**一条**报价拼出结果，`refreshPrices` 就报 `source: 'live'`——其余 25 只票根本没更新，界面却一切正常。现在覆盖率低于一半会报 `error`，pill 会显示故障并触发重试，拿到的那部分报价照常应用。

## 说明

你设备上 Edge Function 调用失败的**根因我还没确定**（最可能是 AdGuard 之类的拦截器挡了 `supabase.co`——README 里记录过 AdGuard 曾经删掉过你的 script 标签）。但现在即使它失败，代理兜底也能给出正确的盘前涨跌，而且真出问题时界面会如实告诉你。

四项检查全绿（581 测试，新增 8 个回归测试），README 已同步。等 Cloudflare 部署完，**在 app 里点 RELOAD 换新 bundle** 后再看。如果盘前还是全 0，告诉我，我再从"为什么 Edge 连不上"这条线查。

### assistant  ·  2026-08-06 18:25:59

这个问题和本仓库无关（这里是投资组合追踪 PWA，没有游戏项目），所以我不清楚你说的是哪个游戏——下面按通用情况讲，最后列出哪些信息会改变我的建议。

## itch.io 是什么

2013 年由 Leaf Corcoran 创立的**独立游戏发行/托管平台**，可以理解成"独立游戏界的 Bandcamp"：

- **零门槛**：注册即可上传，**没有审核、没有上架费**（对比 Steam 要交 $100/款）
- **支持形式**：可下载安装包（Win/Mac/Linux/Android）、**浏览器直接玩的 HTML5 游戏**、以及素材包、工具、音乐、电子书
- **game jam 大本营**：GMTK Jam、Ludum Dare 等几乎都在 itch 上办，这是它最大的流量来源
- **收入分成可自定义**：默认抽 10%，但你可以自己调，**甚至调成 0%**
- **定价灵活**：免费、固定价、"随你付"（pay-what-you-want）都行
- **回款方式**：可配置成买家付款**直接进你的 PayPal/Stripe**，不经过平台账户

## 关于广告和变现 —— 这是最关键的部分

**itch.io 本身不投广告、也没有广告分成。** 它的变现模式只有"卖游戏 / 打赏"。所以影响取决于你现在靠什么赚钱：

**如果你现在靠自己网站挂广告（AdSense 之类）赚钱 —— 要特别小心：**

1. **itch.io 的 HTML5 游戏跑在他们自己域名的 iframe 沙箱里**（不是你的域名）。AdSense 要求你对投放域名有所有权、能在根目录放 `ads.txt`——你在 itch 域名上做不到。**在 itch 托管的游戏里塞 AdSense 极可能违反 AdSense 政策，严重的会封号。**这是最大的坑。
2. **分流问题**：玩家在 itch 上玩，你自己网站的广告展示次数就少了。等于把能变现的流量导到不能变现的地方。

**折中做法**（这是我实际会推荐的）：
- itch 上放**试玩版/demo**，或者干脆只做一个介绍页面，按钮链回你自己的网站玩完整版
- 或者 itch 版做成付费/打赏（无广告体验），自己网站保留免费+广告版——两条线互不冲突

**如果你想要的就是广告分成收入**，itch 不是对的平台，应该看：**CrazyGames、Poki、GameDistribution/GameMonetize、Newgrounds**——这些是广告分成模式，会主动给你流量。缺点是有审核、要接他们的 SDK。

**如果你的游戏是买断制/打赏制**，itch 基本没有坏处，值得传。

⚠️ 提醒：我的知识有截止时间，itch.io 对"HTML5 游戏内嵌第三方广告"的具体条款我**没有十足把握**，上传前请自己核对一遍他们的 [Content Policy](https://itch.io/docs/general/content-policy) 和 Terms。

## 详细提交步骤

**1. 注册**
访问 itch.io → Register → 验证邮箱。如果要收钱，先去 Settings → Payments 绑定 PayPal 或 Stripe。

**2. 创建项目**
右上角头像 → **Dashboard** → **Create new project**

**3. 逐项填写**

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **Title** | 游戏名 |
| **Project URL** | 网址后缀，创建后不好改，想清楚 |
| **Short description** | 一句话简介，显示在列表和分享卡片上 |
| **Classification** | 选 **Games** |
| **Kind of project** | 网页游戏选 **HTML**；有安装包选 **Downloadable** |
| **Release status** | Released / In development / Prototype |
| **Pricing** | `$0 or donate`（免费+打赏）/ `Paid`（定价，可设最低价）/ `No payments` |
| **Uploads** | 见下 |
| **Description** | 页面正文，支持富文本，写玩法、操作说明、更新日志 |
| **Genre / Tags** | Tags **最多 10 个**，这是站内搜索的主要入口，认真选 |
| **Community** | 关闭 / 评论区 / 论坛——建议开评论区收反馈 |
| **Visibility** | 先留 **Draft**，配好了再切 Public |

**4. 上传文件**

- **HTML5**：打包成 **zip，`index.html` 必须在压缩包根目录**（不能套一层文件夹）。上传后勾选 "**This file will be played in the browser**"，然后设置：
  - Viewport 尺寸（填你游戏的实际分辨率，比如 960×540）
  - 勾 **Fullscreen button**
  - 手机能玩就勾 **Mobile friendly**
- **可下载版**：分平台传 zip，并标记对应的 Windows/macOS/Linux 图标
- 单文件大小上限约 1GB（免费账号）

**5. 视觉素材（很影响点击率，别省）**

- **Cover image**：**630×500 px**（最低 315×250）——列表页和分享卡片用的就是它
- **Screenshots**：3–5 张，展示实际玩法画面
- **Trailer**：可填 YouTube/Vimeo 链接

**6. 发布**
Save → "View page" 预览 → 确认无误后把 Visibility 改成 **Public**。

**7. 推广（重要）**
itch.io **自然流量很有限**，别指望传上去就有人玩。真正带量的是：
- 参加 **game jam**（最有效）
- 发 Reddit（r/IndieGames、r/WebGames）、X/Twitter 带 `#indiedev`
- itch 站内的 devlog 功能（每次更新发一篇，会推到关注者）

## 要给你更准确的建议，我需要知道

1. **游戏现在在哪、怎么变现的？**（自己网站挂广告？还是纯免费？）
2. **是 HTML5 网页游戏还是可下载的？**
3. **你的目标是什么**——赚钱、拉玩家、还是单纯找个地方展示作品？

如果是"自己网站 + 广告"这种情况，我倾向于**不要把完整版直接传 itch**，改用上面说的 demo 导流方案。你把情况说一下，我可以帮你把具体方案和页面文案都规划出来。

    const rows = [];
    for (const [ticker, f] of Object.entries(byTicker || {})) {
      const ts = Number(/** @type {any} */ (f)?.earningsDate);
      if (!isFinite(ts) || ts <= nowSec) continue;
      rows.push({
        ticker,
        ts,
        time: /** @type {any} */ (f)?.earningsTime || null,
      });
    }
    rows.sort((a, b) => a.ts - b.ts);
    return rows.slice(0, 3);
  }, [byTicker]);

  return (
    <section className={`panel earnings-panel ${className}`}>
      <h3 className="panel-title">UPCOMING EARNINGS</h3>
      <div className="earnings-list">
        {upcoming.length === 0 ? (
          <div className="earnings-empty mono dim">No scheduled earnings.</div>
        ) : upcoming.map(row => (
          <div key={row.ticker} className="earnings-row">
            <span className="earnings-ticker mono">{row.ticker}</span>
            <span className="earnings-date mono">{fmtEarningsDate(row.ts)}</span>
            <span className="earnings-time mono dim">{fmtEarningsTime(row.ts, row.time)}</span>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

### assistant  ·  2026-08-07 16:47:56

三个都改好推 main 了（commit `b27df40`）。

## 1. UPCOMING EARNINGS 只显示当前持仓

原因是它用的是 `Object.keys(holdings)`。清仓一只票时，代码会把它从各 position 的 `tickers` 里移除，但**故意保留 holdings 那一行**（为了留住买卖台账），所以按 holdings 取就把已卖光的票也算进去了。

改成和表头「N tickers」同一套**板上作用域**（被某个 position 引用的非现金票）。另外加了一道保险：每次渲染都用当前板上的票再过滤一遍——因为 `byTicker` 会保留上一次的响应（拉取失败时更是一直留着），不然盘中卖光的票还会滞留一会儿。

## 2. TOP MOVERS / 战术板显示 SIVE

`displayTicker` 原本只在 `heatmap.jsx` 里。已移到 `formatters.js`，热力图、战术板球员牌、TOP MOVERS 三处共用，所有 `2DG` 变体（`.F` / `.SG` / `.DE`）都显示 **SIVE**。

**个股详情弹窗保持显示真实代码 2DG.SG**——按你的要求，这样你能看清自己持有的到底是哪个交易所的挂牌。

## 3. 弹窗 0% 的原因

`chart_modal_geometry.js` 里 ext 打开时，1D 的锚点取的是「今天的正式收盘价」（`lastPrice`）。这条规则对**美股收盘后**是对的——那时 `lastPrice` 确实是已完成的收盘价。

但 2DG.SG 在美股盘前时段**正在交易**，它的 `lastPrice` 是**实时价**。于是就成了「实时价 ÷ 实时价」= **永远 0.00%**。而热力图那边用的是 `dayPct`（对 prevClose），所以显示正常——两边就对不上了。

修法：外国挂牌股在**自己交易所开市期间**，锚点改用 `prevClose`，也就是热力图用的同一个基准。同时把「这只外国股此刻是否开市」抽成一个共享函数 `foreignSessionIsOpen`，看板和弹窗都调它——**这两处原本各写一遍交易所时钟逻辑，正是它们会漂移的根本原因**。

## 验证

四项检查全绿，588 个测试（新增 7 个）：
- 弹窗锚点：外国股开市中锚 prevClose、无 prevClose 时回退、**美股路径不受影响**（防回归）
- `displayTicker`：`.SG` 等全变体映射 + 空值安全
- 财报面板：已清仓的票不显示，而且**根本不会为它发起请求**

等 Cloudflare 部署完就能看到。盘前那段时间点开 SIVE 详情页，百分比应该和热力图一致了。

## 做了什么

UPCOMING EARNINGS 现在显示 **`RKLB FY26Q2`** 这样的格式，财季跟在代码后面。

## 关键坑：Yahoo 给的季度标签是错的

Yahoo 确实有现成字段 `earningsChart.currentQuarterEstimateDate/Year`，但那是**自然季度**，只有财年=自然年的公司才对得上。我实测过：

| 票 | Yahoo 给的 | 公司自己叫 |
|---|---|---|
| RKLB | 2Q 2026 | FY26Q2 ✓ 恰好一致 |
| NVDA | 2Q 2026 | **FY27Q2** ✗ |
| AAPL | 3Q 2026 | **FY26Q4** ✗ |

直接用会让 NVDA、AAPL、MU 这些非自然财年的公司全标错。所以改成自己推导：用 `earningsTrend` 的季度结束日 + `defaultKeyStatistics.lastFiscalYearEnd`（**这两个模块本来就在同一个请求里，零额外网络开销**）。

推导规则：从财年结束月往后数三个月为一季（结束月当月即 Q4），财年编号取「财年结束所在的自然年」——这正是公司自己的编法。**只看月份不看具体日期**，这样 52/53 周财年（NVDA 今年 1 月 25 号、明年 1 月 26 号）不会飘。

## 验证

拿真实探测数据钉了四种财年类型：RKLB（12月）→ FY26Q2、NVDA（1月）→ FY27Q2、AAPL（9月）→ FY26Q4、MU（8月）→ FY26Q4，**全部与公司官方叫法一致**。

五项检查全绿：typecheck / lint / 589 vitest（+1）/ build / 157 deno（+5）。

## 两点说明

- **后缀是可选的**：Yahoo 没给财年数据的票就只显示代码，不会出现空缺口或错标
- 样式上财季比代码淡一档、字号小一号，窄屏优先让它收缩，不会挤掉日期和 BMO/AMC

Edge Function 部署完（约一两分钟）刷新页面就能看到。

```
export async function fetchFundamentals(symbols, opts = {}) {
  const list = Array.from(new Set((symbols || []).filter(Boolean)));
  if (list.length === 0) return {};
  try {
    const qs = `?tickers=${encodeURIComponent(list.join(","))}`
      + (opts && opts.ttmEpsHistory ? "&ttmEpsHistory=true" : "");
    const url =
      `${EDGE_PRICES_URL.replace(/\/prices$/, "/fundamentals")}${qs}`;
    const res = await fetch(url, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${EDGE_ANON_KEY}`, apikey: EDGE_ANON_KEY },
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000),
    });
    if (!res.ok) return {};
    const data = await res.json();
    return data && typeof data === "object" ? data : {};
  } catch {
    return {};
  }
}
```

function fmtEarningsDate(unixSec) {
  const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', {
    timeZone: 'Europe/London',
    day: '2-digit', month: 'short',
  }).formatToParts(new Date(unixSec * 1000));
  let dd = '', mo = '';
  for (const p of parts) {
    if (p.type === 'day') dd = p.value;
    if (p.type === 'month') mo = p.value;
  }
  return `${dd} ${mo}`;
}
=== fmtEarningsTime ===
function fmtEarningsTime(unixSec, timeName) {
  if (typeof timeName === 'string' && timeName.length > 0) {
    const lower = timeName.toLowerCase();
    if (lower.includes('before')) return 'BMO';
    if (lower.includes('after'))  return 'AMC';
  }
  const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', {
    timeZone: 'Europe/London',
    hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', hour12: false,
  }).formatToParts(new Date(unixSec * 1000));
  let hh = '00', mm = '00';
  for (const p of parts) {
    if (p.type === 'hour') hh = p.value;
    if (p.type === 'minute') mm = p.value;
  }
  return `${hh}:${mm}`;
}

## 当日财报保留到当天结束：已修复并推 main（`8d869fe`）

原来的过滤条件是 `earningsDate <= now`，所以 21:00 的财报**一到 21:00 就消失**——恰恰是财报数字刚出来、你最想看的时候。

改成比较**伦敦日历日**（和这一行日期、时间渲染用的是同一个时区），当天的财报会一直留到那一天真正结束。

另外顺手处理了一个边界：日期键改成每次渲染重算并纳入 memo 依赖，这样 PWA 挂着过夜时，列表会在午夜后一个刷新周期内自动翻页，而不是卡在挂载那天。

四项检查全绿（590 个测试，新增 1 个：验证「今天 21:00 已过的财报仍显示、昨天同一时刻的不显示」）。

等这次部署完，**完全退出 app 再打开**，财季和当日保留应该会一起生效。

  const { winners, losers, positionList } = React.useMemo(() => {
    const allPlayers = [];
    for (const pos of Object.values(metrics.positions)) {
      for (const p of pos.players) allPlayers.push({ ...p, pos: pos.label });
    }
    const movable = allPlayers.filter(p => !p.isCash && p.ticker !== "CASH");
    // Only names that ACTUALLY moved rank. A row pinned at 0 — a no-US-ext
    // venue suppressed during the overnight (SFTBY / .L / euro / CN fund), or
    // a genuinely flat stock — is neither a winner nor a loser, so it must not
    // pad either column (the overnight LOSERS list was five red 0.00% rows).
    // Show however many really gained / fell, up to 5 each.
    return {
      winners: movable.filter(p => (p.dayPct ?? 0) > 0).sort((a, b) => (b.dayPct ?? 0) - (a.dayPct ?? 0)).slice(0, 5),
      losers:  movable.filter(p => (p.dayPct ?? 0) < 0).sort((a, b) => (a.dayPct ?? 0) - (b.dayPct ?? 0)).slice(0, 5),
      positionList: Object.entries(metrics.positions)
        .filter(([_, p]) => p.players.length > 0)
        .sort(([, a], [, b]) => b.marketValue - a.marketValue),
    };
  }, [metrics]);

 *
 * @param {{ positions: Record<string, any>, holdings: Record<string, any> } | null | undefined} p
 */
export function portfolioUserFingerprint(p) {
  if (!p || typeof p !== 'object' || !p.holdings || !p.positions) return '';
  const parts = [];
  for (const k of Object.keys(p.positions).sort()) {
    const pos = p.positions[k] || {};
    const tickers = Array.isArray(pos.tickers) ? [...pos.tickers].sort() : [];
    parts.push(`p:${k}=${pos.role || ''}|${pos.label || ''}|${pos.subtitle || ''}|${tickers.join(',')}`);
  }
  for (const t of Object.keys(p.holdings).sort()) {
    const h = p.holdings[t] || {};
    const lots = Array.isArray(h.lots)
      ? h.lots.map(l => `${l?.date || ''},${l?.shares ?? ''},${l?.cost ?? ''}`).join(';')
      : '';
    parts.push(`h:${t}=${h.shares ?? ''}|${h.cost ?? ''}|${h.currency || ''}|${!!h.isCash}|${lots}`);
  }
  return parts.join('\n');
}

CORS does NOT prevent\n    // that — it only constrains browsers, not curl — so the token is\n    // the actual control. Checked BEFORE any upstream call so a\n    // rejected request costs nothing.\n    const appToken = req.headers.get(\"x-app-token\") ?? \"\";\n    if (!(await verifyToken(appToken))) {\n      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: \"invalid token\" }), {\n        status: 401,\n        headers: { ...CORS, \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n      });\n    }\n'''\nfor fn, anchor in [\n    (\"prices\", '    const url   = new URL(req.url);'),\n    (\"chart\", None),\n    (\"fundamentals\", None),\n]:\n    p = f\"supabase/functions/{fn}/index.ts\"\n    s = open(p).read()\n    # 1) allow the header through preflight\n    s = s.replace('\"Access-Control-Allow-Headers\": \"authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type\"',\n                  '\"Access-Control-Allow-Headers\": \"authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type, x-app-token\"', 1)\n    # 2) import verifyToken\n    if 'verifyToken' not in s:\n        m = re.search(r'^import .*?;\\n', s, re.M)\n        s = s[:m.end()] + 'import { verifyToken } from \"../_shared/token.ts\";\\n' + s[m.end():]\n    # 3) insert the gate right after the OPTIONS early-return\n    m = re.search(r'\\n([ \\t]*)if \\(req\\.method === \"OPTIONS\"\\) \\{\\n.*?\\n\\1\\}\\n', s, re.S)\n    assert m, f\"{fn}: OPTIONS block not found\"\n    s = s[:m.end()] + \"\\n\" + GATE + s[m.end():]\n    open(p, 'w').write(s)\n    print(f\"{fn}: gated\")\nPY",

## 已修（`b92f1f9`）

**#1 热力图/战术板 vs Top Movers** — 找到了：三个界面各自判断「算不算变动」。热力图把 `|pct| < 0.005`（也就是显示成 0.00% 的）当持平画成灰块，Top Movers 却用裸的 `> 0 / < 0` 排名。所以截图里 **MSFT** 同时是「深灰无变动块」**和**「红色跌幅榜 −0.00%」。三处统一走 `pctIsFlat`。

**#5 指纹漏 sells/closed** — 同意，而且是真实的数据丢失。已平仓的持仓 shares=0/cost=0，所有被指纹覆盖的字段都一样，改卖出日期/价格 = 指纹不变 = 保存被当成 no-op。已加入 `sells`（含 ts）和 `closed`，pin 测试覆盖「改已平仓持仓的卖出日期必须改变指纹」。

**#6 addHolding 抹台账** — 同意，且**比 flag 说的更严重**：它整个重建 holding 对象，`lots`、`sells`、`closed` 全丢。改成 `mode` 参数：`append`（追加买入，从完整台账重算股数/均价）/ `replace`（重述持仓，`.PVT` 重新估值依赖它）。两种模式都保留 sells/closed，重复添加时用**现成的 useConfirm** 弹窗让你选。

**#7 写死 2025-01-01** — 同意。改成当天。理由和 flag 一致：lots 是 YTD 的真相来源，早于 1 月 1 日 = 「去年就持有」，这个常量每过一年就把回填持仓错分类一次。

**#9 类型脱节** — 加了 `sells` / `closed` / lot+sell 的 `ts`。`loadAuth`/`saveAuth` **我没删**——它们确实没有调用方，但和这批 bug 修复无关，混在一起会让 diff 更难审。

**#13 硬编码重复** — 已改走 `supabase_config.js`。

## 已修（`b193e78`，单独一个 commit）

**#4** — 我**部分不同意** flag 的方案：

- **锁 CORS 没用**。`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` 只约束浏览器，curl 和服务端脚本完全无视它。「防白嫖」这个威胁，锁 CORS 挡不住。而且收紧 origin 反而有搞挂 preview 部署的风险。所以 CORS 我保持 `*`。
- **token 才是真正的控制**。prices / chart / fundamentals 现在要求和 `data` 一样的 `X-App-Token`，且在任何上游调用**之前**校验。同时把 `x-app-token` 加进三个函数的 `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`（不加的话预检会失败，整条数据链会挂——这是这个改动最容易踩的坑）。healthcheck 里那三个改成期待 401。

我把它单独提交，就是因为它影响整条实时数据链：万一出问题，可以单独回滚而不影响前面那批 bug 修复。

## 我没做的两条

**#10 拆 app.jsx** — 同意问题存在（`doRefresh` 280+ 行确实难审），但这是纯重构、零用户可见收益、回归风险高，不该和 bug 修复捆在一起推。而且你现在还有个未解的线上问题（PWA 缓存），重构会让新旧行为对比更难。建议单独做，我可以下次专门开一轮。

**#12 不提交构建产物** — 同意方向，但**我做不完**：改用 Cloudflare 构建需要你在 CF Pages 控制台里设置 build command 和 output directory，我没法从这里改。你把 CF 那边配好，我再改仓库这边（删产物 + 更新 .gitignore + 调 CI）。

## 需要你注意

`b193e78` 部署后，**如果你的 PWA 还是旧 bundle**，它不会发 `X-App-Token`，所有行情会 401。所以这次更新后**务必完全退出 app 再打开**。这也正好能当作一次验证——新版行情正常 = token 链路通了。

### assistant  ·  2026-08-17 01:33:59

已推 main（`05f8e4a`）。

## 改动

输入 `.5` 现在会自动补成 `0.5`。我把它应用到了**弹窗里全部 8 个小数输入框**，不只是股数——买入成本、卖出股数、卖出价、现金金额、添加股票的均价/最新价，这个简写习惯对它们同样自然，只修一个反而会让其他框显得不一致。

## 关键约束

`normalizeDecimalInput` **只处理开头的那个点**，别的一律原样返回。因为它跑在每一次按键上，最重要的是**不能在你打字打到一半时跟你抢**——比如输入 `12.75` 的过程中会经过 `12.`，如果normalizer在这一步"帮你修"就没法用了。所以：

- `.5` → `0.5`，`.` → `0.`，`-.5` → `-0.5`
- `0.`、`1.`、`12.75`、空字符串 → 原样不动

顺带说明：这纯粹是**显示层**问题，计算一直是对的（`Number('.5')` 本来就等于 0.5），只是框里看着别扭。

## 验证

除了纯函数的单测，我还加了**真实按键测试**——在弹窗里逐字键入 `.5`，断言框里显示 `0.5`、保存下去的值是 `0.5`；再断言 `12.75` 全程不被打断。这一步很必要：这些是受控输入，一个会破坏受控状态的 normalizer 可以轻松骗过纯函数测试，但实际用起来是坏的。

四项检查全绿（611 个测试，新增 7 个）。

做对的
#5 指纹 — 实现和理由都对。sells（含 ts）+ closed 打进 fingerprint，正好打中「已平仓、shares/cost 全是 0」这条丢失路径。pin test 也对准了这个失败模式。
#1 pctIsFlat — 热力图、Top Movers 现在走同一个 0.005 阈值，MSFT 那种「灰块 + 红榜 −0.00%」会消掉。pctColor 里本来就是 Math.abs(n) < 0.005，数值一致。
#7 回填日期 — 改成当天是对的。已有的 2025-01-01 lot 不会被改写（只填空），这点也对：别去动已经存进去的账。
#13 配置去重 — yahoo_fetch 走 supabase_config 没问题。
#4 CORS vs token — 这里 Claude 比我原先的建议更准。Access-Control-Allow-Origin 只约束浏览器，curl / 脚本完全无视。真正的控制面是 token。他做对了三件具体的事：
	•	在打 Yahoo / Finnhub / AV 之前 验 token（拒了不烧配额）
	•	三个函数的 CORS 预检都加了 x-app-token（不加整条链会挂）
	•	healthcheck 改成期待 401
historical.js 的 /chart、fetchFundamentals 也都带上了 header，调用点没有漏。
#10 / #12 先不做 — 同意。纯重构、零用户收益，还不该和 bugfix 捆；CF 控制台你得自己配，他改不了。
#9 不删 loadAuth — 也同意，别把无关清理塞进这批 diff。

不同意 / 有坑
1. 买入日期被吃掉了（这次引入的回归）
AddTickerModal 会传第 5 个参数 buyDate：
onAdd(ticker, shares, cost, lastPrice || cost, buyDate);
app.jsx 里新回调只收 4 个，然后显式传 undefined：
onAdd={async (ticker, shares, cost, lastPrice) => {
  // ...
  addHolding(addingToPos, ticker, shares, cost, lastPrice, undefined, mode);
}}
YTD 依赖 lot 日期。用户在「Buy date」里选的日子现在全部变成今天。这是这次改动带进来的，应该马上补：
onAdd={async (ticker, shares, cost, lastPrice, buyDate) => {
  addHolding(addingToPos, ticker, shares, cost, lastPrice, buyDate, mode);
}}
2. 确认框把「取消」映射成了「覆盖」
const addMore = await askConfirm({ confirmLabel: 'Add purchase', cancelLabel: 'Replace position' });
mode = addMore ? 'append' : 'replace';
addHolding(...); // 无论选啥都会执行
useConfirm 里 Esc、点遮罩、点 Cancel 全是 false。用户以为在取消，实际会走更危险的 replace，而且 Add 弹窗也会被关掉。
这不该是二元 confirm。至少：
	•	false = 中止，什么都不写
	•	两个并列按钮都是正向操作（「追加」/「覆盖」），没有「取消 = 覆盖」
3. `replace` 保留 sells，但股数不走 `netPosition`
测试里写得很清楚：lots 换成新的一笔，sells 留下，shares 用输入值。于是：
	•	卖掉 2/10 再 replace 成 8 股 → 板上 8，台账 8 − 2 = 6
	•	清仓后再买入、手滑选了 Replace（或按了 Esc）→ closed: true 还在，sells 还在；下次在 Edit 里随手 Save，updateHolding 会按 netPosition(新lot, 旧sells) 再算一遍，仓位可能直接变 0 / 负数再被平掉
.PVT 重估没有 sells，那条路径没事。问题出在「卖光再买回来」。
更干净的语义：
	•	append：追加 lot，按完整台账重算（现在这样就对）
	•	replace：lots 和 sells 一起重述（真的「这就是当前仓位」），并清掉 closed
	•	或者 replace 也跑 netPosition，别让板上数字和台账打架
4. 「旧 PWA 会全盘 401」说重了
Edge 401 之后，yahoo_fetch / historical 仍会掉到 CORS proxy。价格多半还能亮，只是变慢、吃公共代理配额。会空的是没有 fallback 的 fundamentals（财报面板、P/E）。
硬刷 PWA 仍然该做，但更准确的说法是：新版函数先于新 bundle 上线时，旧客户端会变慢、财报空，不是整板死掉。 部署顺序最好是：先确认 Pages 新 bundle 出去，再让 Edge 强制 token；或者接受一段时间双轨。
5. Token 门禁的强度 = 密码强度
现在从「有 anon key 就能白嫖」收成「有 admin/ro 密码才能打」。这是对的。但如果密码还是 4 位数字，RO 口令被撞开后，代理通道照样开着。token 是必要的，替代不了换口令。

一句话
工程判断好：该修的修了，该拆的拆了，CORS 的反驳成立。上线前先补 buyDate，再把确认框改成「取消 = 不写」——这两处是这次 diff 自己引入的
